page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.6xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 12 physical cores supplying 24 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with simultaneous multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. Memory architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 KB of L1d cache. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. System memory totals 24.0 GB RAM, yielding a lean allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU core. The server lacks attached local storage and dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on external block storage while providing an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface.

Benchmark evaluations reflect solid multi-threaded execution balanced by lower single-core efficiency. Multi-core processor performance falls into average tiers across standard testing, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 7777.0, a multi-core stress-ng rating of 17725.14, and a PassMark CPU score of 18361.58. Multi-core software compilation with Clang achieves a score of 14738.0, while static web serving delivers 13.45 GB/sec throughput. In contrast, single-core processing performs in lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1009.0 and weak single-threaded compression throughput. Cached memory read bandwidth reaches 987.8 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block writes yield 37.21 GB/sec.

Given its high vCPU count relative to memory capacity, ecs.ic5.6xlarge offers a cost-effective platform for compute-dense workloads that do not require extensive memory footprints. Architectural tradeoffs include low per-core memory overhead and modest single-threaded responsiveness, making it less suitable for memory-heavy databases or execution paths reliant on single-core speed. However, its 24 vCPUs excel in parallel processing tasks such as multi-threaded batch compilation, distributed web serving, lightweight key-value caching (handling 17.02 million Redis SET operations per second), and small-scale parallel data processing.
